EvanDan55:

@Foote: Who is better (in your opinion): Scorpion or Sub-Zero?

This might be the toughest question I'v ever been asked in my life… Shoot, I'm gonna have to be wishy-washy here.

For me, it comes down to what kind of gamer I want to be at that moment. Scorpion is a fantastic blitz-type attacker. You need to stay in their face and keep the pressure on. Scorpion has a way of dictating the pace of matches because your opponent has little choice but to constantly play to counter your "GET OVER HERE". If you miss a pull as Scorpion you are screwed, but both you and your opponent know that, you can use that to your advantage. Forcing you opponent to play reactionary instead of to their strengths is huge in the meta-game of it all, and Scorpion does that unlike any other MK character.

Sub-Zero is a perfect foil to Scorpions perfered style. SubZero is all about baiting, counters, and feining reactionistic play. Against a blitzer like Scorpion, ice clones are always a chief concern which forces close range characters to put more space between you. At mid range Zero can throw just about anything at you and is where he opperates the best. Once you land that first good counter on an opponent, its game over from a mind-game perspective. Mistakes are punished rather hard with this style of play, so you're gonna need good timing to pull it off.

Given perfect play by each character head to head, my money is on SubZero. Though it is far easier to brute force wins with Scorpion with spam Pull-Stuns.

posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
Of course, asking if a letter has friends is an absurd question, but to some extent, it does not matter who we are talking about, the question of whether or not it is possible for anyone or anything to have a friend is by itself interesting.

 

To describe one as a friend is to make a statement about a relationship. Labeling one as a friend implies some combination of past actions, current feelings, and likely future actions. We could discuss the various actions or feelings that different people might characterize as being friendly. I think it suffices to say that the definition of being a friend changes from person to person. So, while defining what it means to be a friend would be a quite a complicated task and change depending on the individuals involved, I'm willing to posit that there is such a thing as friendship and that it can be reasonably reliably recognized.

 

But is it real?

 

I don't mean to engage in a debate about what is reality. I'm not asking about whether the universe really exists or whether we just think it does. I'm asking whether what we think of as friendship, in terms of past actions, current feelings, and future actions -- which we regularly see on a day to day basis -- is real.

 

The mind is complicated thing. How much of your life do you really remember? How much of the actions that you take are taken conciously? Do we really have friends, or do we just happen to act in certain ways? Is there a difference?

 

Ok, I admit it. I think we really have friends, but I think there's still a useful point here. I think the vast majority of the time we are on autopilot and it is only in rare instances that we are truly present and aware of what's going on. So, a lot of the time, we don't really have friends, because to some extent we're asleep. It's only in the ephemeral when we take conscious action that we truly exist.

 

I'll think about what question I want to ask ...

posts.cooked:
Well, my forum name isn't that interesting a story really - it involves an old RPG character and an email address, but I'll give you a little more detail. 

It's 1997. I'm at school studying for A Levels, and I'm 17. My friend L starts dating D, who is possibly the geekiest person I've ever met. He's your stereotypical nerd - big glasses, gangly, poor social skills, mad hair, extremely intelligent, awkward, and besotted with L who doesn't yet realise that they are not at all suited to each other (incidentally, both are now happily married to other people). D attends a roleplaying club on Friday nights, and asks L to go with him. She asks me to go too, and because I'm a good friend I agree I'll go to keep her company. I plan to make some excuse to avoid it after that first time because it sounds a bit weird, to be honest.

And so begins my roleplaying career. At the club I meet some interesting people, and the gaming bug bites me pretty hard, beginning with a diceless Nightlife game and then moving into AD&D where the DM gives me a fighter who comes from a slightly magical pirate family who all share the same bright red hair and the surname Red. I give her the unimaginative first name Scarlett, and play her for years. I actually miss her, and should recreate her some time. 

I end up in a relationship with D's best friend C who also attends. We start going to LARP events, and I convert Scarlett to that system, and we decide, as LARPing couples often do (it's very embarrassing) to have an in-character wedding. The shame of it. Everything's arranged, but C manages to get his character killed just before the ceremony and I impress people with my acting skills, being able to actually cry over it (this is a skill I no longer have at all).

A little later I need a new email address, since my old Hotmail one is impossible to use anymore because no-one knew how to avoid getting spammed to death back then. I choose my new web mail provider, but scarlettred is unavailable. I can't think of anything more imaginative so I steal C's character's surname because I'm an idiot, and it just happens to be Silverleaf. And Scarlett Silverleaf sounds okay, I guess. 

I've used it on the internet ever since, but fairly quickly found that people called me Silverleaf or Silver rather than Scarlett. And now I'm used to it, and it's my primary 'net name and has been for a long time.

See, not very interesting.
